newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa futures rise late to end slightly up.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa futures rise late to end slightly up.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures gained late on Wednesday to close slightly higher after spending most of the day softer and in a tight range.

July edged up two stg to 1,021 stg per tonne and September gained two to 1,039. Total volume tallied a sluggish 1,625 contracts, with July grabbing the largest share. July notched 463 trades, followed by December's 397.
Options volume remained non-existent at nil.

Traders said 214 against actuals (AAs) traded, mostly in July and some in September. Further turnover came from July/September switches. Traders said 50 of those switches traded at 19 stg earlier in the day.
Otherwise, activity was dull, and traders said the quiet could last until the end of the month when more crop and weather information is revealed.

Some traders were also looking to New York's first notice day in a few weeks to help push cocoa out of its range. They said speculative selling there related to first notice day could provide a temporary spike lower.
Until then, July was likely stay in a range between about 1,000 and 1,035.

Some traders expected July to stay buoyant and continue inching up toward the top end of its trading range but others said with volume so low, July could easily shed another five to ten stg by Friday solely on lack of interest.
